messages.content:
Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: Why would Two ETFs tracking Identical Indexes Produce different Returns?\nassistant: Even if two ETFs are tracking the same index, they can still produce different returns due to varying management fees and expenses. This is because these costs can eat into the returns of the ETF, causing a discrepancy in the total returns between two funds. However, from an investor's point of view, the nominal prices of the tracking funds are not important. What matters is that when the underlying index moves by a given percentage, the price of the tracking funds should also move by an equal percentage. Any small difference in total returns will be attributable to these management fees and expenses, which is why low fees are so important in passive investing.  Index fund and ETF returns are all publicly available so you don't have to guess.\nuser: Average fees\nassistant: While a typical expense ratio  for mutual funds is 1% (annualized real rate of return on the stock market - after inflation - is about 4%), ETFs like SPY (which reflects the S&P 500 index) have a much lower annual expense ratio, such as .09% or VOO, with its .05%.   Since there are both good and bad ETFs, buying only $1000 at a time the broker transaction fee will eat too much of your money. You want to keep such fees way down below 0.1%.\nuser: 1% ratio annualized real rate is 4%?",
    "answer": "不是。这里的意思是：股票市场扣除通胀后的年化实际回报率约为4%，而基金的典型费用率为每年1%。因此，1%的费用约等于4%实际回报的四分之一，会显著减少投资者的净收益。文档还提到，Vanguard的典型费用率约为0.1%–0.2%。（根据第1页）"
}
Output:

statements: 1%指的是基金的典型年度费用率，而不是股票市场的年化实际回报率。
股票市场扣除通胀后的年化实际回报率约为4%。
基金的典型费用率为每年1%。
每年1%的基金费用约相当于4%年化实际回报的四分之一。
基金费用会显著减少投资者的净收益。
根据文档第1页，Vanguard的典型费用率约为0.1%至0.2%。
